nodes.label: One Mail Identity
nodes.rationale: Four mails are composed by one module with one identity: Arcula <noreply@arcula.art> as sender, Arcula <hello@arcula.art> as Reply-To when EMAIL_REPLY_TO is set, the hosted wordmark, one call-to-action with the same URL in the text part, a line saying why the message arrived, and no tracking pixel.

nodes.label: Hosted Wordmark arcula-name-logo.png
nodes.rationale: The wordmark is apps/web/public/arcula-name-logo.png — the one the SPA serves, not a second copy — and it is the only image a mail carries.

nodes.label: Dev Reply-To Left Empty on Purpose
nodes.rationale: Dev has no monitored inbox and the code never invents an address; the invitation footer offers a reply only when a Reply-To is configured and otherwise says the mail can be ignored, so it never promises a person behind an unmonitored address.

nodes.label: DMARC Reporting Then Enforcement
nodes.rationale: The record currently is v=DMARC1; p=none with no reporting, so there is no evidence of what fails and nothing stops forgery. The staged path is p=none with rua → p=quarantine → p=reject over weeks. Dev gets its own _dmarc.dev.arcula.art at p=none so production's enforcement never catches dev. Do not add ruf and do not rely on pct (poorly supported). This is a DNS change on reports, not a release, so never bundle it with a deploy.

nodes.label: Email Opt-Out Deferred Until Complaints
nodes.rationale: The four mails are two account mails and two relationship notices, which Resend's guidance treats as exempt, so no opt-out ships and no mail promises one; revisit if deliverability insights show complaints. The shape when built: an email_opt_outs table keyed by normalised address, an HMAC token, RFC 8058 one-click GET/POST, List-Unsubscribe headers on invitation mail only, invitation create and resend refusing a suppressed address, account mail and the transfer notice never suppressed so an account can always recover, and the migration shipping in its own release.
